audit.reasoning: Coding of record: excluded (undetermined-sources) after the first audit showed StressTyp2's 'initial primary + 3R secondary' misreads its own source. Verified on held pages: Klimov 1999 p. 54 says the mirror image (2-3σ initial; polysyllables MAIN stress antepenult, SECONDARY initial; stress 'weakly expressed'); Harris 1991 §1.3 (Gudava 1969, Senak) gives a right-edge C-final-penult / V-final-antepenult rule with contrastive pairs and 'considerable variation'; Kipshidze 1914 §7 p. 013 (held, read on the page image) gives antepenult but alternatively a double stress with the MAIN stress word-initial, and calls the stress very weak outside interrogatives. sources.quote: p. 8: 'In the Senaki dialect of Megrelian, the stress window consists of the penultimate and antepenultimate syllables (Gudava 1969). Stress is penultimate in consonant-final words, and antepenultimate in vowel-final ones. Exceptionally, some vowel-final verbs … have penultimate stress, which leads to minimal pairs: dóɣuru … doɣúru (Gudava 1969: 109).' p. 23: 'Stress properties of Megrelian are contested … little instrumental data is available. sources.locator: preprint p. 8 (§4.2 stress windows) and p. 23 (§7.2 Kartvelian, Megrelian paragraph)

sources.citation: Poniava, Natia. 2020. Word Stress in Megrelian. International Journal of Multilingual Education 15: 33-42. ISSN 1512-3146. CC BY-NC 4.0. https://multilingualeducation.openjournals.ge/index.php/ijml/article/view/6737
sources.quote: p. 33 (abstract): 'In the scientific literature there is no common view regarding the position and nature of stress in Megrelian. Our study is based on experimental analysis. The experiment has revealed that in Megrelian, in two-syllable and three-syllable words the stress is on the initial syllable. However, in some case the stress falls on the penultimate syllable in three-syllable words. As for four-syllable words, the stress is on the antepenult though our experiment did not confirm the presence of the secondary stress. In five-syllable words the primary stress falls on the second syllable
sources.locator: abstract p. 33; lit. review pp. 33-35; Table pp. 36-38; conclusion p. 40
sources.note: The only instrumental study of Megrelian word stress (18 speakers, 9 municipalities); states outright that the literature has no common view and finds weak stress with a length-dependent locus (σ1 at 2-3σ, σ2 at 4-7σ) matching none of Kipshidze/Klimov/Gudava/StressTyp2 — the quotable modern authority for the exclusion, which currently carries no quote at all.
